body:
i merged this one yesterday to try mitigate the JS/source map end without getting too invasive, and it seemed to help somewhat, but might need a bit more work. https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/5208

See also https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5223 as we're likely to be re-orging this

I was _so_ happy that we can run this bundling in parallel :-) But yeh, if it gives trouble to our build infrastructure we can easily re-shape it to do things sequentially. Provided that we are sure that this is the root cause, of course.
it might be enough to just refactor the code bundle sequentially instead of using `Q.all`.

I have a pending PR of the new system builder, that allows separation
between the tracing step and the writing to disk step. It definitely is
much faster and lighter weight. Coming soon.
On Fri, Nov 13, 2015 at 12:11 Igor Minar notifications@github.com wrote:

> it might be enough to just refactor the code bundle sequentially instead
> of using Q.all.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5229#issuecomment-156544561.

Just in case it helps. I think this trace might be related to this issue. Running `gulp build` on OS X El Capitan with node v4.2.4 :

```
[12:38:10] Starting '!bundle.testing'...

<--- Last few GCs --->

  113851 ms: Mark-sweep 1380.6 (1456.9) -> 1383.2 (1456.9) MB, 1259.5 / 0 ms [allocation failure] [GC in old space requested].
  115110 ms: Mark-sweep 1383.2 (1456.9) -> 1383.2 (1456.9) MB, 1258.9 / 0 ms [allocation failure] [GC in old space requested].
  116382 ms: Mark-sweep 1383.2 (1456.9) -> 1378.1 (1456.9) MB, 1272.0 / 0 ms [last resort gc].
  117639 ms: Mark-sweep 1378.1 (1456.9) -> 1379.9 (1456.9) MB, 1256.3 / 0 ms [last resort gc].


<--- JS stacktrace --->

==== JS stack trace =========================================

Security context: 0xf6261cb4629 <JS Object>
    2: _serializeMappings(aka SourceMapGenerator_serializeMappings) [/Users/alfonso/Workspace/angular/node_modules/systemjs-builder/node_modules/source-map/lib/source-map/source-map-generator.js:~289] [pc=0x111d3ae2115e] (this=0x1b111ff80b59 <a SourceMapGenerator with map 0x21a7c3960b41>)
    3: toJSON(aka SourceMapGenerator_toJSON) [/Users/alfonso/Workspace/angular/node_modules/systemjs-builder...

FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST Allocation failed - process out of memory
Abort trap: 6
```

It doesn't happen if I only run `gulp build.js`

Contributing a failure for `gulp build.js`. On node v4.2.1 El Capitan 16GB RAM.

```
[01:06:42] Starting '!bundle.testing'...

<--- Last few GCs --->

  140814 ms: Scavenge 1374.7 (1455.7) -> 1374.7 (1455.7) MB, 3.5 / 0 ms (+ 1.7 ms in 1 steps since last GC) [allocation failure] [incremental marking delayin
g mark-sweep].
  142008 ms: Mark-sweep 1374.7 (1455.7) -> 1296.6 (1455.7) MB, 1194.1 / 0 ms (+ 3.1 ms in 2 steps since start of marking, biggest step 1.7 ms) [last resort g

c].
  143279 ms: Mark-sweep 1296.6 (1455.7) -> 1296.6 (1455.7) MB, 1271.4 / 0 ms [last resort gc].


<--- JS stacktrace --->

==== JS stack trace =========================================

Security context: 0x3e0e73637399 <JS Object>
    2: _serializeMappings(aka SourceMapGenerator_serializeMappings) [/Users/stephenbussey/personal/angular/node_modules/systemjs-builder/node_modules/source-
map/lib/source-map/source-map-generator.js:~289] [pc=0x13217c8fd240] (this=0x2b5a4f0e72d1 <a SourceMapGenerator with map 0x37c172fd5261>)
    3: toJSON(aka SourceMapGenerator_toJSON) [/Users/stephenbussey/personal/angular/node_modules/syste...

FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST Allocation failed - process out of memory
[1]    95243 abort      $(npm bin)/gulp build.js
```

This script seems to do the trick, however.

```
node --max-old-space-size=2000 ./node_modules/.bin/gulp build.js
```

@pkozlowski-opensource is looking into this. I don't think that we'll be able to reduce the memory usage easily without impacting the total build time, so let's increase the heap size by default when calling `gulp build.js` (or more specifically the bundle task that causes the OOM).

This will require spawning a new process from within the gulp process but that should be a big deal. We just need to make sure that it's done a cross-platform compatible way.

Why not allocate more memory to the entire gulp process, rather than start a sub-process? Is it to avoid parts of the build outside of bundling that start to rely on more available heap?

One solution is to use npm run-scripts in the `package.json` so the memory settings are saved with the gulp command to run, eg

```
"scripts": {
  "build": "node --max-old-space-size=2048 ./node_modules/.bin/gulp build.js"
}
```

(I'm trying this now because I have the same issue on Circle, which already uses `npm run build` rather than shell scripts as the build step)
